svg.title: Neoplasia decision chart: a mass is pre-malignant while the basement membrane is intact (dysplasia, carcinoma in situ) and malignant once through it, then staged by how it spread (direct T, lymphatic N, hematogenous M) and graded by differentiation; each column gives what defines it, how it is found and what it means

svg.text: A MASS: is it a neoplasm, is it MALIGNANT, and how far has it SPREAD?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: describe it first: size, shape, surface/borders, colour, consistency

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: a mass is NOT always cancer: it may be a cyst, abscess, blood or fluid

svg.text: SPREAD is the one criterion · stage it by HOW it spread: tumour, node, metastasis (TNM)

svg.text: GRADE it by how the cells look: well differentiated (I, slower) → poorly or UNDIFFERENTIATED (immunohistochemistry
